title_en: SPECIAL ANNOUNCEMENT: Capital Allocators University Online
title_zh: 特别公告：Capital Allocators University 转为线上按需课程
subtitle_zh: Ted Seides 与 Hank Strmac 对谈，解读 CAU 六大模块、目标学员与课程搬到线上的三层考量。
summary_zh: 本期 Capital Allocators 是一则特别公告，主持 Ted Seides 与公司 CEO Hank Strmac 对谈，宣布把 Capital Allocators University（CAU）从一年一期、每期 25-30 人的线下学习小组（cohort）改造为线上按需课程（on-demand），并保留一年一度的线下聚会。CAU 教授的是一系列对提升投资业绩极重要、却在 MBA 或 CFA 课堂学不到、通常只能边干边学的学科，六大模块涵盖访谈技巧、公众演讲、决策、领导力与管理，以及现代投资框架。Seides 以彼得原理（Peter principle）说明为何出色的分析师升任 CIO 未必懂领导与管理，并举决策卫生（decision-making hygiene）为例：Kahneman 与 Tversky 的研究多停留在诊断偏差，而 Annie Duke 的《Thinking in Bets》、Michael Mauboussin 的梳理才提供了『怎么做更好』的工具；他自己做播客九年、经历几百次访谈，才总结出哪些提问技巧有效。课程最适合资产端 5 到 15、20 年经验的从业者，也向上覆盖到 CIO，并因伙伴 Rahul Moodgal 的启发延伸出面向投资者关系（IR）与商业开发者的版本——发现公众演讲与访谈技巧对两边同样适用。转线上有三层考量：内容值得反复听、社交不必绑定在一整天课程上、降价后个人也能自费参加；成品由 Fondue 团队以 masterclass 质感打磨。整体呼应 CAU『让知识与关系同时复利』的使命。
description: SPECIAL ANNOUNCEMENT: Capital Allocators University Online

turns.en: I'm Ted Sides, and this is Capital Allocators. I'm excited to share something we've been working on for a while. We're bringing Capital Allocators University online.
turns.zh: 我是 Ted Seides，这里是 Capital Allocators。很高兴和大家分享一个我们做了很久的事——我们正在把 Capital Allocators University（资本配置者大学，CAU）搬到线上。

turns.en: For years, CAU has been an in-person once-a-year cohort of 25 or 30 professionals built around a set of disciplines that matter enormously for investors and investor relations professionals, but rarely get taught explicitly.
turns.zh: 多年来，CAU 一直是一年一期、每期 25 到 30 位从业者的线下学习小组（cohort），围绕一系列对投资人和投资者关系（investor relations）从业者极其重要、却很少被明确教授的学科来设计。

turns.en: Hank and I put together a brief conversation to share more on what the course covers, who it's for, what we've learned from the past five years, and why we decided to move it on demand.
turns.zh: 我和 Hank 一起录了一段简短的对话，跟大家更多地介绍这门课涵盖什么、面向谁、过去五年我们学到了什么，以及为什么决定把它做成按需（on-demand）课程。

turns.en: If you want the full details, the modules, the pricing, and how to sign up, there's a link in the show notes, where you can head to capitalallocators.com and look for university.
turns.zh: 想要完整信息——模块设置、价格和报名方式——节目笔记里有链接，你可以访问 capitalallocators.com，找到 university 页面。

turns.en: We look forward to having you involved and hope you enjoy this brief special announcement on our new online Capital Allocators University. Ted, these special announcements are always fun to do because it means we've been busy.
turns.zh: 我们期待你的加入，也希望你喜欢这段关于全新线上 Capital Allocators University 的简短特别公告。Ted，每次录这种特别公告都很有意思，因为这意味着我们最近又忙出了新东西。

turns.en: Before we set the stage and give the background on Capital Allocators University, why don't you explain what we're doing as to not bury the lead?
turns.zh: 在我们铺垫背景、介绍 Capital Allocators University 的来龙去脉之前，你先讲讲我们到底要做什么吧？别把最重要的新闻压在后面。

turns.en: Yeah. We're moving Capital Allocators University online. The course up until now has been an in-person once-a-year cohort that was usually 25 or 30 people.
turns.zh: 好。我们把 Capital Allocators University 搬到线上了。在此之前，这门课一直是一年一期、通常 25 到 30 人的线下学习小组。

turns.en: We decided to bring it on demand alongside of an attached annual gathering so that people can access it when they want and get the benefits of coming together.
turns.zh: 我们决定把它做成按需课程，同时配一场一年一度的聚会，这样大家既能在需要的时候随时学习，又能享受到面对面交流带来的好处。

turns.en: What is Capital Allocators University and how did it come to be? The course itself is a series of disciplines that I think are incredibly important for improving investment results, but are not the things you learn in an MBA course or the CFA.
turns.zh: Capital Allocators University 到底是什么？它是怎么来的？课程本身讲的是一系列学科，我认为它们对提升投资业绩极其重要，但在 MBA 课堂或者 CFA（注册金融分析师）课程里是学不到的。

turns.en: There are things that I started picking up from doing podcast interviews, but weren't things I'd been exposed to in my 20 years investing. You could think about things like interviewing techniques, something I've had to spend a lot of time thinking about the last nine years, and a bunch of other things like that where they might be disciplines taught in most businesses, but they're not taught in investing.
turns.zh: 这些东西是我做播客访谈时才开始一点点学到的，在我 20 年的投资生涯里根本没接触过。比如访谈技巧——过去九年我花了大量时间琢磨这件事——还有好多类似的学科，也许在别的行业里有人教，但在投资行业没人教。

turns.en: A lot of learning on the job from these types of disciplines. If it happens at all in most cases, it generally doesn't happen because they're not necessarily well-known of the track, the classic Peter principle that someone gets promoted to the point of their incompetence.
turns.zh: 这类学科大多只能边干边学。多数情况下根本没人去学；即便有人学，也谈不上体系化、有章法——就是那句经典的彼得原理（Peter principle）：一个人被不断提拔，直到升到他自己不胜任的位置。

turns.en: A great investment analyst becomes a portfolio manager, becomes someone who's a chief investment officer. That doesn't mean they've learned how to lead people and manage people.
turns.zh: 一位出色的投资分析师升成组合管理人，再升成首席投资官（CIO），这并不意味着他学过怎么领导别人、管理别人。

turns.en: It's not part of the skill set that they got brought up in. Some of the people have never been exposed to it to give a frame of reference. What are the six modules of Capital Allocators University?
turns.zh: 这些本就不在他们一路成长时习得的技能清单里，有些人更是从来没接触过。给大家一个参照框架——Capital Allocators University 的六大模块分别是什么？

turns.en: There's interviewing techniques, public speaking, decision-making, leadership and management, and there's one on modern investment frameworks.
turns.zh: 有访谈技巧、公众演讲、决策、领导力与管理，还有一个模块讲现代投资框架。

turns.en: When we originally put the cohort and the curriculum together, who was it intended for? We started doing it during COVID. It was virtual, and as soon as we could move in person, we did, and we didn't know it first.
turns.zh: 我们当初组建学习小组、设计课程的时候，是想面向谁？我们是在新冠疫情期间起步的，一开始是线上，一能恢复线下就马上转成了线下。说实话，一开始我们也没摸准。

turns.en: In fact, our first cohorts had everyone from a CIO down to someone just getting into the business. We had the range of people, and what we honed in on the right person was someone with several years' experience in the seat because we weren't teaching the investment basics.
turns.zh: 最初几期，学员从 CIO 到刚入行的新人都有，跨度非常大。后来我们逐渐锁定：最合适的人是那些在岗位上干了好几年的人，因为我们教的不是投资基础。

turns.en: Some of these things, you can't apply until you're in a position where you've learned a few things. You're not going to lead people and manage people as a junior analyst, as an example.
turns.zh: 这些东西里，有些必须等你坐到某个位置、已经学过一些东西之后才用得上。举个例子，初级分析师是不需要领导和管理团队的。

turns.en: We've had several CIOs come through it and get a lot out of it, so it does go all the way up. What we found was it was somewhere between five and 15 or 20 years of experience was the right range on the allocator side.
turns.zh: 我们也确实有几位 CIO 上过课、收获很大，所以它向上也能覆盖到顶端。我们发现，在资产端，最合适的是 5 年到 15、20 年经验这个区间。

turns.en: Within each of these disciplines, how did we put together the curriculum for these disciplines that you've outlined? In any liberal arts education, there's a certain set of fundamental principles that if you dive in and learn them, they become a body of knowledge.
turns.zh: 在你刚才说的每一个学科内部，课程是怎么搭起来的？任何博雅教育（liberal arts education）里都有一组基本原理，你钻进去把它们学透，它们就成了一整套知识体系。

turns.en: I always love that phrase. The CFA uses that for the body of knowledge of investing, or the CFA course teaches all the basics of investing. Some of these are things that I picked up from other people.
turns.zh: 我一直很喜欢“知识体系”这个说法。CFA 就用它来指投资的知识体系，CFA 课程教的就是投资的全部基础。这里有些内容是我从别人那里学来的。

turns.en: Some of them I picked up from practice, and some of them I connected the dots and you start hearing the same thing over and over and you realize that's a discipline.
turns.zh: 有些是我从实践中摸出来的，有些是我自己把点连成线——当你开始反复听到同一件事，你就会意识到：这是一门学科。

turns.en: As an example, decision-making practice, good decision-making hygiene is a relatively new body of knowledge. For the last 15, 20 years, people became familiar with behavioral biases, all the condominant toversky work.
turns.zh: 举个例子，决策实践、良好的决策卫生（decision-making hygiene）是一套相对较新的知识体系。过去 15、20 年，大家熟悉了行为偏差，熟悉了 Kahneman 和 Tversky 的全部研究。

turns.en: But most of that just prescribed the problem, didn't tell you what to do about it. The first time I saw anybody take that and say, here are some tools you might use to get better, whether no one's going to be good at this or hardwired to get it wrong, was Annie Duke's thinking in bets.
turns.zh: 但那些研究大多只是诊断了问题，没告诉你该怎么办。我第一次看到有人在此基础上说出“这里有一些工具可以让你做得更好”——毕竟没人生来就擅长决策，也不是注定会犯错——就是 Annie Duke 的《Thinking in Bets》。

turns.en: That was influential to me. I became friends with Annie, had her on the show several times in learning how do you try to make better decisions, both as an individual and with a team.
turns.zh: 这本书对我影响很大。我和 Annie 成了朋友，请她上节目好几次，一起学习怎么做出更好的决策——既包括个人决策，也包括团队决策。

turns.en: That's a great example of something that started with Annie's work and then trying to learn more about it. People like Michael Mobison are great at curating a lot of knowledge about that as well.
turns.zh: 这正是一个很好的例子：从 Annie 的工作出发，然后继续深挖。像 Michael Mauboussin 这样的人，在梳理和集成这方面知识上也做得非常出色。

turns.en: Different example, interviewing. I suppose I've been interviewing managers for 20 years before I started the podcast, but I tell people I didn't think about was I doing well as an interviewer.
turns.zh: 再举一个不同的例子——访谈。在做播客之前，我采访基金经理大概也有 20 年了，但我跟别人说过，我以前从没想过：作为一个访谈者，我做得好不好？

turns.en: The podcast and the feedback loop that came from editing and having it go out forced me to listen to myself asking questions. I started to realize, well, that was a bad question or why did I ask this question at this point in time?
turns.zh: 播客带来的反馈闭环——剪辑、节目发布——逼着我去听自己是怎么提问的。我开始意识到：那个问题问得不好，或者，我为什么在这个时间点问这个问题？

turns.en: So I've had now nine years, if several hundred reps of a very specific type of interviewing and from that learned certain techniques that work and don't.
turns.zh: 到现在九年，相当于几百次非常特定类型的访谈练习，从中我总结出哪些技巧有效、哪些没用。

turns.en: And then I went and tried to study other great interviewers like Charlie Rose, Larry King, Tim Ferriss. And you start to learn people have different styles.
turns.zh: 然后我又去研究其他伟大的访谈者，比如 Charlie Rose、Larry King、Tim Ferriss，慢慢你会发现每个人都有不同的风格。

turns.en: A journalist has a different style from a podcast interviewer. And you find your own style, but in each style there are certain common disciplines.
turns.zh: 新闻记者的风格和播客访谈者不一样。你要找到自己的风格，但每种风格里都有一些共通的学科规律。

turns.en: So just share what those are. And some of those are just connecting the dots. And folks who are in an allocator seat aren't listening to themselves hundreds of times over interviewing a manager.
turns.zh: 所以我们只需要把这些讲清楚就好。其中有些道理就是你把线索连起来。坐在配置岗位上的从业者，从来不会听自己采访经理人的录音几百遍。

turns.en: There's a big part of this that you start to realize that people ask you the same questions over and over. The first time I experienced that was when I was leaving investing in small hedge funds and a new startup hedge fund manager would come in and literally ask the same questions that I'd been answering for 10 years.
turns.zh: 这件事很大程度上是你开始意识到：别人会反复问你同样的问题。我第一次有这种体会，是在我要离开小型对冲基金投资的时候。一位新创办的对冲基金经理来见我，问的问题和我过去 10 年回答过的简直一模一样。

turns.en: And so I decided I didn't want to do that anymore, but I'd put it together in a book and so people could read about it. And it's the same stuff that applies today.
turns.zh: 于是我决定不想再这样一遍遍回答了，就把它们整理成一本书，让大家可以直接去读。书里那些东西放到今天依然适用。

turns.en: And I think that's right when you're really busy and you're in it in investing. You don't have time to take a step back and try to study these disciplines, try to make sure what works.
turns.zh: 我觉得这很正常——当你忙于一线投资的时候，根本没有时间退后一步去研究这些学科，去分辨什么才是有效的。

turns.en: The nice thing about doing the podcast is I'm not in it. I don't have to spend time doing due diligence and mercifully, I don't. But that gives me some time to be able to study other things that are very relevant for investors.
turns.zh: 做播客的好处是，我不再身处其中。我不必再花时间做尽职调查，谢天谢地也不用。但这就给了我一些时间，去研究那些对投资人真正相关的其他事情。

turns.en: What were some of the main takeaways from the folks that participated in the cohort? There were two, one expected and one unexpected. The expected was that the course material was incredibly rich and dense.
turns.zh: 参加过学习小组的人，主要的收获是什么？有两点，一点在意料之中，一点在意料之外。意料之中的是，课程材料极其丰富、极其密集。

turns.en: In any one of these 20 minute modules, there might be 15 different takeaways. Hard to digest all at once. The second which I suppose we could have anticipated but didn't realize and appreciate the power is that cohort, that people that are five to 15 years of experience don't have as many networking opportunities as CIOs or senior decision makers that are regularly going to annual meetings and meeting their peers.
turns.zh: 随便哪一个 20 分钟的模块里，都可能有 15 条不同的要点，一次消化完很难。第二点——按理说我们本可以预料到，但当时并没有真正意识到和领教它的力量——就是学习小组本身：5 到 15 年经验的人，不像 CIO 或资深决策者那样经常参加年度会议、会见同行，他们的社交机会少得多。

turns.en: So it was very valuable for those people to be able to get together and meet each other and have people to talk to in the industry. Each of those went into taking what we were doing and trying to make it more broadly available.
turns.zh: 所以，让这些人能聚在一起、彼此认识、在行业里有人可以交流，对他们非常有价值。这两点都推动我们把手上的课程做得更普惠、覆盖更多的人。

turns.en: Can you speak a little bit to the application of these frameworks? We heard and what we found about taking all these learnings that we throw at people in a single day and how they apply it to their actual job and their actual teams.
turns.zh: 你能不能谈谈这些框架的实际应用？我们听到、也发现的一个问题是：一天之内灌输给学员这么多内容，他们到底怎么把它用到实际工作和实际团队里？

turns.en: There are two aspects of that. The first is the most important thing was doing it. We'll teach a bunch of frameworks and then we learn to give homework.
turns.zh: 这有两层。第一层，最重要的是要去做。我们会讲很多框架，后来我们学会了留作业。

turns.en: Hey, make this like a class. And the people who did the homework consistently would come back to us and say they got more out of Cape Ellicors University than the ones who hadn't.
turns.zh: 对，把课程像正式课堂那样来上。那些一直认真做作业的人回来告诉我们，他们从 Capital Allocators University 的收获比不做作业的人多得多。

turns.en: They can't just listen to, hey, I'm telling you, this is a good thing to try to do. Go do it. And if you integrate it piece by piece, that was the first.
turns.zh: 不能只是听人说“嘿，我告诉你，这是件值得尝试的好事”。要真的去做，一点一点把它内化，这是第一层。

turns.en: The second is there's a lot of stuff. Hearing it once wasn't as valuable for the people. We record them and then put them on our website for the people who came to the course.
turns.zh: 第二层，内容太多了，只听一遍对大家的价值有限。我们会把课程录下来，放到网站上给来过的人回看。

turns.en: And the ones who went back and said, oh, I listened to it again and I pulled another thread and I pulled another thread, got more out of it than the people who just showed up and listened once.
turns.zh: 那些回来说“我又听了一遍，又扯出一根线头、再扯出一根线头”的人，收获远大于只来听一遍的人。

turns.en: All of what you've described and the disciplines you've outlined were originally intended for the asset allocator. Where did we pick up the idea to do the cohort for investor relations along the way?
turns.zh: 你刚才描述的这一切、列出的这些学科，最早都是面向资产配置者的。我们中途是怎么想到要为投资者关系从业者也开一期学习小组的？

turns.en: That started with our partner, Rahul Udgal, who's in that seat and kept saying over and over, we need to do this for IR people. They don't have that network of peers and there's a lot that they don't understand about how allocators think.
turns.zh: 这要从我们的伙伴 Rahul Moodgal 说起，他自己就在这个岗位上，反复跟我们说：我们得为 IR 从业者也开一门课。他们没有同行网络，对配置者怎么思考也有很多不了解。

turns.en: We put together a course two years ago, decidedly for investor relations and business development professionals to help them understand how allocators think, help them get a whole bunch of different tips from different people who are great in the seat.
turns.zh: 两年前我们专门搭建了一门课，明确面向投资者关系和商业开发从业者，帮他们理解配置者的思维方式，帮他们从那些在这个岗位上非常出色的人那里学到各种实用技巧。

turns.en: And we've done that twice in person as well. One of the things we learned too by doing that course that was so fascinating was how applicable some of the frameworks and disciplines we'd put together for allocators were to the investor relations professional, the public speaking techniques, even the interviewing techniques, being on the receiving end of an allocator interview, it was really useful context and training for them to have from those respective disciplines.
turns.zh: 这门课我们也线下开了两期。通过这门课我们发现的另一件特别有意思的事是：我们原本为配置者搭建的那些框架和学科，用在 IR 从业者身上同样适用——公众演讲技巧，甚至访谈技巧，因为他们要坐在配置者访谈的接收端。这些学科给他们提供了非常有用的背景和训练。

turns.en: One of the things you hear when you listen is that the best investor relations people, the best salespeople are far more listeners and question askers than the stereotype would tell you that they are.
turns.zh: 你听得多了就会发现，最优秀的 IR 从业者、最优秀的销售，比人们刻板印象里更善于倾听、更善于提问。

turns.en: The whole idea of interviewing is not only applicable, it's essential for someone who's in that seat to thrive. So yeah, some of those disciplines are equally valuable across both.
turns.zh: 访谈这套学问不仅适用，对于想在这个岗位上如鱼得水的人来说更是必不可少的。所以，没错，这些学科对配置者和 IR 两边同样有价值。

turns.en: So what then prompted the decision to move this curriculum to an online on-demand format? There are three aspects of it, only two that matter.
turns.zh: 那么是什么促使你们把这套课程转成线上按需形式的？这有三层原因，其中两层才真正重要。

turns.en: One was the value that people got from repeatedly hearing the module and I'm going to listen to it 10 times, but when I do a podcast, I end up listening to it three times.
turns.zh: 第一层，大家从反复听同一个模块中获得的价值。我不会说“我要听它 10 遍”，但像我这样做播客，最后也会不由自主地听三遍。

turns.en: I do the actual interview, I'm involved in the editing, I listen when it comes out and I can internalize more of the lessons from that by more than a multiple of three.
turns.zh: 我完成访谈、参与剪辑、节目上线后再听一遍，我能吸收的经验远不止一遍的三倍。

turns.en: But sometimes it takes a little bit of repetition to make it available so it's easy for someone to go in and listen when it's valuable to them was better than you have to come to New York this day once a year.
turns.zh: 但有时候，内容需要靠一点重复才能真正吸收。所以让内容随时可听、让大家在对自己最有价值的时候进去听，总好过规定你每年必须来一次纽约、只能在这一天上课。

turns.en: We wanted to make it more broadly available because we had a lot of people that were interested in coming but couldn't come that one time and they're like, okay, well now you have to wait till the next year.
turns.zh: 我们想让它惠及更多人。很多人想来，但偏偏那一次来不了，结果就只能“好吧，那再等明年”。

turns.en: That was the first. The second part was that networking piece, which is so valuable to those people, doesn't have to be attached to sitting down and listening to a whole set of modules over the course of the day.
turns.zh: 这是第一层。第二层是社交这件事——对那些人来说价值巨大——但它并不非得绑定在“花一整天坐下来听完一整套模块”上。

turns.en: So we could bring those two together and as a part of that, we'd bring this cohort of people together and they'd get together once. We all know if you have a cohort of people, if you get to see them more than once, you build the relationships better.
turns.zh: 我们可以把这两件事结合起来：把这批学员聚在一起，先聚一次。我们都知道，一批人如果能见不止一次面，关系会建立得更好。

turns.en: So we said, if we make it so that everyone has come to the course, can come to a gathering each year, that becomes a more powerful network. The third, which might not be relevant to some, was by bringing it online, we could significantly reduce the price point and make it more available.
turns.zh: 所以我们想：如果让上完课的人每年都能来一场聚会，这张网络就会更有力量。第三层，对有些人可能不那么相关——搬到线上之后，我们可以大幅降低价格，让更多人上得起。

turns.en: When we were doing it in person to put it on, to rent a place, it cost more money. It became a corporate expense. It was hard for it to be an individual expense.
turns.zh: 做线下的时候，租场地、办下来花的钱更多，它就变成了一笔公司开支，个人很难自己掏钱来上。

turns.en: By bringing it online and being able to lower the price point, it could be either. People can go and get it paid for by their company, but they also can do it individually and we thought that would make it available to more people.
turns.zh: 搬到线上、价格降下来之后，两种都行。你可以让公司报销，也可以自费。我们觉得这样能覆盖更多人。

turns.en: Why don't you give a sense of how that ultimately came together? How did we create what is now this Capital Caterers University online? We spent a day in the studio with a team called Fondue who did incredible work with us.
turns.zh: 你能不能讲讲最后是怎么打磨出来的？我们是怎么打造出现在这个线上版 Capital Allocators University 的？我们和一个叫 Fondue 的团队在工作室录了一整天，他们配合我们做了非常出色的工作。

turns.en: We recorded these modules one by one. We had an audience for half of it. I sat in front of a teleprompter for half of it and I didn't use the teleprompter, but I was in front of it.
turns.zh: 我们一个模块一个模块地录。有一半是当着观众录的，有一半我坐在提词器前面——虽然我没用提词器，但我确实坐在它前面。

turns.en: It was very strange. Then we worked with Fondue to make them into what feels like a high quality masterclass, very much like the masterclass series.
turns.zh: 那种感觉很奇怪。然后我们又和 Fondue 一起，把成品打磨成一种高品质的 masterclass（大师课），非常像 MasterClass 那个系列。

turns.en: If I could expand on that further, Fondue was a partner in creating what is the content that you'll ultimately consume from the online module.
turns.zh: 我可以再补充一点：Fondue 是内容创作上的伙伴，你们最终在线上模块里消费到的那些内容，是他们一起参与打造的。

turns.en: They were responsible for the video production, but also what the final output ultimately ended up looking like and feeling like they did a phenomenal job.
turns.zh: 他们不仅负责视频制作，最终成品看起来、听起来是什么质感，也出自他们之手——他们做得非常棒。

turns.en: For those who are interested in getting involved, how can they do so? Hop on our websites, capitalcaterers.com, look for a university and sign up.
turns.zh: 感兴趣的朋友怎么参与呢？上我们的网站 capitalallocators.com，找到 university 页面，直接报名。

turns.en: You'll immediately get access to all the online courses whenever you want. Once a year, we'll bring everybody together, really looking forward to doing that.
turns.zh: 报名后你立刻就能访问全部线上课程，随时想学就学。每年我们还会把大家聚到一起，这一点我们非常期待。

turns.en: I think what's exciting is this is an initiative that directly ties to our mission of compounding knowledge and relationships for its social asset owners and investment firms.
turns.zh: 我觉得最让人兴奋的是，这个项目直接呼应了我们的使命——为机构资产所有者和投资公司实现知识与关系的复利。

turns.en: It is compounding knowledge with the curriculum of these disciplines that you've put together and relationships by getting one together once a year.
turns.zh: 你搭起来的这套学科课程，就是在让知识复利；每年大家聚一次，就是在让关系复利。

turns.en: I think that's spot on. We're excited to bring this to more people, which is the real rationale for bringing it online. Excellent. Well, Ted, it's good to give this context.
turns.zh: 说得完全对。我们很高兴能把这门课带给更多人，这正是我们搬到线上的真正原因。很好。嗯，Ted，把这些背景讲清楚真的很好。

turns.en: We're excited for this new project and we look forward to having you involved. Thanks for listening to the show. If you like what you heard, hop on our website at capitalallocators.com, where you can access past shows, join our mailing list, and sign up for premium content.
turns.zh: 我们对这个新项目很兴奋，也期待你的参与。感谢收听本节目。如果你喜欢这期内容，请访问 capitalallocators.com，那里可以回看往期节目、加入我们的邮件列表，并订阅付费内容。

turns.en: Have a good one and see you next time. All opinions expressed by Ted and podcast guests are solely their own opinions and do not reflect the opinion of capital allocators or their firms.
turns.zh: 祝大家一切顺利，我们下期再见。Ted 和各位播客嘉宾表达的所有观点仅代表其个人观点，不代表 Capital Allocators 或其所在机构的立场。

turns.en: This podcast is for informational purposes only and should not be relied upon as a basis for investment decisions. Clients of capital allocators or podcast guests may maintain positions and securities discussed on this podcast.
turns.zh: 本播客仅供参考，不应作为投资决策的依据。Capital Allocators 或播客嘉宾的客户可能持有本节目中讨论到的证券头寸。
